'''''Ulex minor''''', the '''dwarf furze''' or '''dwarf gorse''' is an [[evergreen]] [[Chamaephyte|dwarf shrub]] in the family [[Fabaceae]], native to eastern [[England]], [[France]], [[Spain]] and [[Portugal]]. It is restricted to lowland [[Heath (habitat)|heathland]] habitats.

It normally grows about {{Convert|30|cm|in|sigfig=1}} tall, although in shaded, un[[grazing|grazed]] conditions it may reach {{Convert|1|m|in|sigfig=1}}. It is a low-growing shrub, forming small bushes or often growing mingled with [[Calluna|heather]].  The [[leaf|leaves]] are limited to scales or small spines, and the [[Shoot (botany)|shoot]]s are modified into rather soft, green, densely crowded [[spine (botany)|spine]]s, about {{convert|1|cm|in|sigfig=1|abbr=on}} long.

The [[flower]]s are yellow, {{Convert|1|–|2|cm|in|sigfig=1|abbr=on}} long, with the typical [[pea]]-flower structure; they are produced principally in the late summer and autumn, rarely before July. The [[fruit]] is a [[legume]] (pod), partly enclosed by the pale brown remnants of the flower.

Due to its relatively soft spines, dwarf furze is readily [[Grazing|grazed]] by [[livestock]] and wild [[herbivore]]s.

The distributions of dwarf furze and its close relative western gorse (''[[Ulex gallii]]'') hardly overlap, even in similar habitats.
